# 1. Executive Snapshot

- **Cheap, fast "subagent" models arrived.** Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 is reported (aggregators, Oct 8) at roughly 75% below Haiku 4.5 pricing, with a 1M-token context and computer-use gains. High-volume agent work (triage, extraction, classification) just got materially cheaper.
- **Databases are being rebuilt for agents.** Supabase raised $150M (led by GIC, with CapitalG; Oct 2) and agreed to acquire Turso (SQLite-based, built for very large numbers of isolated small databases), four months after a $500M Series F at a $10.5B valuation.
- **Agents are moving onto the desktop.** NVIDIA and Microsoft described co-engineering for agents running on Windows PCs (Oct 7), alongside a reported GPT-6 rollout with interactive "Intelligent UI" in ChatGPT (single source, unconfirmed).
- **Risk:** the control standard for agents is still unwritten (open since Oct 4) while capability and deployment surface keep growing. Cheaper agents mean more of them, faster.
- **Recommended attention level: Medium.** One cost-driven experiment (Haiku-class model on a real workload) and one governance action; nothing else needs a project.

# 2. Technologies Worth Watching

**Technology:** Small agent-tier models (Claude Haiku 5.5)

**Category:** AI

**What happened?**
Anthropic reportedly released Haiku 5.5, positioned for subagents and high-volume work. Reported figures: from $0.10 per million input tokens, 1M context, effort controls, 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1 (all from secondary sources; not verified on Anthropic's pricing page).

**Why it matters?**
Agent systems typically spend most tokens on routine steps. If a small model handles those and a larger model only plans and reviews, unit cost falls sharply. This is the practical lever for making agent features economical.

**Business Value:** Lower per-task AI cost; more tasks become worth automating.

**Company Relevance:** 70

**Priority:** High

**Recommendation:** Pilot (route one existing high-volume AI task to the small model and compare quality and cost)

**Expected Impact:** Short

---

**Technology:** Agent-native databases (Supabase + Turso)

**Category:** Cloud / Data

**What happened?**
Supabase will add Turso's technology for provisioning huge numbers of isolated databases cheaply. Stated aim: databases for agent-driven workloads (per-agent or per-task sandboxes). Deal price undisclosed; Turso keeps operating independently for now.

**Why it matters?**
Giving each agent or tenant its own database is a clean isolation and rollback model, and it supports the governance posture buyers are starting to expect. It also signals Postgres-centric vendors are racing to own the agent data layer.

**Business Value:** Isolation, cheap test/branch environments, simpler per-customer data separation.

**Company Relevance:** 50 (higher if we already use Supabase or SQLite)

**Priority:** Medium

**Recommendation:** Observe (acquisition not closed; watch for product details and migration terms)

**Expected Impact:** Medium

---

**Technology:** On-device / desktop agents (NVIDIA + Microsoft, Windows)

**Category:** AI / Enterprise

**What happened?**
NVIDIA and Microsoft outlined joint hardware and software work for agents running locally on Windows PCs.

**Why it matters?**
Local agents can touch files, browsers and credentials on employee machines. That widens the endpoint security surface and makes endpoint management part of agent governance.

**Business Value:** Potential latency and privacy gains; no cloud inference cost for some tasks.

**Company Relevance:** 40

**Priority:** Low

**Recommendation:** Observe (no products to evaluate yet; include endpoint agents in the control standard)

**Expected Impact:** Long

# 3. New Tools & Platforms

**Tool:** Claude Haiku 5.5 (via API)

**Category:** AI

**What does it do?**
Low-cost, fast model for subagent and bulk workloads, with adjustable effort.

**Who should use it?**
Engineers running classification, extraction, summarisation, ticket triage or tool-calling subagents.

**Business Use Case:** Replace a larger model on the highest-volume step of an existing pipeline.

**Estimated ROI:** High if volume is meaningful (reported ~75% lower cost than the prior small tier; confirm).

**Recommended Experiment:** Pick one task, build a 100-item labelled test set, run both models, compare accuracy, latency and cost. Adopt if quality loss is under an agreed threshold.

**Estimated Evaluation Time:** 1-2 days

---

**Tool:** Supabase (agent-oriented database direction, post-Turso)

**Category:** Data

**What does it do?**
Managed open-source Postgres platform; Turso adds lightweight per-agent/per-tenant databases.

**Who should use it?**
Teams building multi-tenant products or agent features needing isolated state.

**Business Use Case:** Prototype per-customer or per-agent isolated data for an internal tool.

**Estimated ROI:** Medium; mainly reduced engineering time on isolation and test environments.

**Recommended Experiment:** Defer the Turso piece; if we use Supabase already, test branching for a staging environment this month.

**Estimated Evaluation Time:** 1 day

# 4. Global Technology Direction

**Where is the market moving?**

- **Cost per agent step is collapsing at the bottom of the stack.** Labs now ship a tiered family (frontier for planning, small for volume). Differentiation moves from raw model quality to orchestration, evaluation and cost routing.
- **Data layer competition.** Cloudflare (Basin/K2, reported Oct 8), Supabase+Turso and AWS are each claiming "where agents keep state." Open formats (Iceberg, Postgres, SQLite) are the common counter to lock-in.
- **Capital keeps flowing to AI infrastructure.** Crunchbase-cited data puts AI at about 64% of Q3 global venture funding; large rounds this week included Supabase, Instinct ($1B Series C), FieldAI ($700M) and a reported Mistral $3.5B Series D (low-reliability source). Expect aggressive vendor roadmaps and more consolidation by acquisition.
- **Agents spreading to endpoints.** Cloud agents (Dots) and desktop agents (Windows) both expand the places an agent can act, which is why regulators and customers focus on control and logging.

**Strategic implications:** Cost is no longer the main barrier to agent adoption; control is. Teams that can route workloads across model tiers and prove agent behaviour will ship faster and pass security reviews more easily.

## What This Means For Our Company

1. Build a model-routing habit now: small model by default, larger model on escalation. It is a cheap change with immediate savings.
2. Keep data in portable stores (Postgres, SQLite, Iceberg); do not commit to a vendor's agent-specific storage yet.
3. The agent-control standard must cover cloud agents, desktop agents and database access. Writing it is now the gating item for everything else.
